Meet our headteacher

Welcome to Denham Green Academy. I am delighted to be the Headteacher of this wonderful academy.
Denham Green is a thriving, successful and happy academy. We are an inclusive academy that proudly serves the needs of our pupils and the local community. Our vision is to ensure that every child who joins us is safe, successful and happy learners who achieve their potential and develop a love of learning.
We value children of all skills and abilities and we provide an environment where they can fulfil their potential and grow into responsible, confident and active young people.
We offer an inspiring, rich and fulfilling teaching and learning environment. The academy consistently performs above the national expectations.
Our academy is a caring and friendly place with an atmosphere of calm and purposeful learning. Children are treated as individuals; we recognise and celebrate different abilities, aptitudes and interests and believe that everyone can develop with self- belief, dedication and hard work. We aim to create a love of learning and a resilience that is essential for achieving excellence. We work hard to ensure every child is happy, safe and successful – a credit to themselves, their family and Denham Green.
Our website offers a glimpse into life at our academy – a caring and supportive community where everyone is encouraged to thrive and reach their potential.
You will be able to find out who we are, what we do and how to find us! It is also a useful way of catching up with all the latest academy news, information and updates.
The best way to find out about us is to come and see for yourself. We always welcome visits from all families and would be delighted to show you around. We look forward to hearing from you soon.
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. As such we expect all staff, volunteers and visitors to share this common commitment.

Pupil leadership
pupil leadership
We strongly believe that preparing the children for the next phase of their education includes offering pupil leadership opportunities where we can. Children are either elected by peers or by the teaching staff based on their suitability for the role, maturity and responsibility. Below are some of the examples of pupil leadership here at the Academy.
Head Boy & Head Girl (with Deputy Head Boy/Girl)
Staff elect the Head Boy and the Head Girl for the Academy from Year 6. The role of the Head Boy and Girl is to act as ambassadors for the Academy when we have visitors here, and will join us in meeting with representatives form the local community as well as the Trust; just this half term alone, our Head boy and Girl have shown prospective parents around the school on our Open Day tours as well as having lunch with one of our Trustees, giving them the pupil perspective on our Academy!
Here at Denham Green we make every effort to consider pupils’ opinions and as a result we operate a School Council which is made up of elected pupils from every class. Meetings are held between the School Council members and chaired by Ms Ashley. The School Council also meets regularly with the headteacher to discuss any suggestions that have been made by pupils.
Our School Council aims to encourage our children to:
· Develop confidence and responsibility and make the most of their abilities
· Prepare them to play an active role as citizens
· Develop healthy, safer lifestyles
· Develop good relationships and respect the differences between people
· To have a “voice” and to share their opinions and ideas with others
We value the benefits of operating a School Council. The School Council represents the whole school. We feel they benefit the whole community and as a school we operate as a community. Through our School Council and class council work it is hoped that we can develop a balance and wholeness, helping to make our community more harmonious to live in. Our School Council work will enable pupils
with positive attitudes to exert a positive influence. Everyone will benefit from the work of the School Council.
Our School Council aims to ensure our children have:
· A safe, happy and fair learning environment
· A forum to voice their concerns and act upon them
· A structured opportunity to learn problem-solving skills
· An opportunity to take an active role in the organisation of the school
· An opportunity to experience a democratic process
Class elections will be held every year. so that different representatives can put forward their election speeches as well as developing the full potential of the School Council to complete tasks. Two candidates will be elected from each class.
Giving Feedback to Pupils:
Following the School Council Meeting, School Council Members speak to their class to let them know what is going on and tell the class about the issues being discussed and what is happening next. This will encourage more children to contribute to further meetings, share worries and let members know the things which could be done to improve the school. The school will record School Council Achievements on the school newsletter as and when appropriate.
Our house captains serve as leaders and representatives of their specific ‘house’ (Air, Earth, Fire and Water) within the Academy’s house system. Their roles may include:
1. Leadership: Guiding and motivating fellow house members to participate in events and activities, such as on Sports Day. Supporting in Key Stage 1 and Nursery Sports Days.
2. Organization: Coordinating practices, meetings, and events related to their house, such as sports competitions.
3. Encouragement: Fostering a sense of team spirit and camaraderie, encouraging participation and enthusiasm among pupils in their ‘house’.
4. Representation: Representing their house in events.

Academy Meals and Aspens
Why School Meals are great
Healthy and Nutritious Lunches
We know that enjoying a nutritious hot meal at lunchtime is always better value than a packed lunch. It is easy to work out how much money you will save by not having to buy and make up packed lunches every day and for the time you save every morning too.
Another important factor is that the meals Aspens serve are nutritionally balanced and they provide a choice of healthy meals.
Our meals are £2.53 per day and freshly cooked and delivered to the site by our caterers Aspens. We have healthy options available each day and have themed meal days too such as Italian day.
Children in Reception to Year 2 are eligible for Universal Free School Meals. If you think your child may be entitled to free school meals from Years 3-6, please let the office staff know and we can discreetly run the checks for you.
If you would prefer your child to have a packed lunch, then please provide a nutritionally balanced lunch. If you do prefer your child to have a hot meal, then please note there is not an option to drop this off for your child at lunchtime and you will need to pay for a hot lunch.
We promote a healthy eating programme at the academy and advise that you provide a healthy lunch for your child. We encourage foods that are healthy:
Food that are not allowed in the school:
Please ensure your child does not bring these items into the academy as they will be confiscated and returned at the end of the academy day.
If your child is eligible for ‘free school meals’ and you register them for this, we will receive extra funding called ‘pupil premium’. We use this extra money to improve the educational provision and resources at the school. We have theme days throughout the year and offer varied and nutritious options for meals. You also could access other future funding and support.
If you meet the criteria below, then please apply as soon as possible for your child to be able to access healthy hot school meals:
How to apply for free school meals
You can apply to register your child for a free school meal and you can check immediately if your child is eligible on https://pps.lgfl.org.uk/. Please speak with the administration office for support with applying. The Academy can also access additional pupil premium funding to support every child who is registered as having access to Free School Meals.
Does my child have to eat the free school meals?
No. Pupils who are registered for free school meals do not have to eat them. If you are eligible but you want your child to have a packed lunch you should still register because the school will receive the funding which can support your child in other ways.
Universal Infant Free School Meals
If your child is in Reception, Year 1 or Year 2, then your child is entitled to Universal Infant Free School Meals which is separate to Free School Meals. Please ensure that you still apply for Free School Meals, so we can access the additional funding to support your child.

Supporting our SEND pupils
At Denham Green E-Act Primary Academy we strive to support all children to enable them to reach their potential at school.
In order to achieve this many steps are taken to support them through their learning journey.
Quality teaching is vital; however for some children there are occasions when additional support may be needed to help them achieve their targets.
At Denham Green E-Act Primary Academy, we believe every child should be challenged to reach their potential. Some children may have needs which are different from, and additional, to their peers and therefore may require additional support or intervention to achieve their potential.
Each pupil’s education programme will be planned by the class teacher. It will be differentiated accordingly to suit the pupil’s individual needs. This may include additional general support by the teacher or teaching assistant in class.
The inclusion manager meets regularly with the team to ensure good practice is shared and any arising issues are addressed quickly.
Learning support assistants support alongside the teacher in the classroom and when appropriate lead small group and one to one intervention to meet individual needs.
If a pupil has needs related to more specific areas of their education, such as spelling, handwriting, numeracy and literacy skills etc. then the pupil will be placed in a small focus group.
This will be run by the teacher or teaching assistant. The length of time of the intervention will vary according to need but will generally be for a term. The interventions will be regularly reviewed by all involved to ascertain the effectiveness of the provision and to inform future planning.
At the academy, we have a dedicated team whom work closely with the teaching staff to support children with additional needs.
Our Special Educational Needs Coordinator is Mrs Claire Kilyan who can be contacted on 01895 833369. She is also our Inclusion Team Lead.
We have a strong team who are well equipped to meet the needs of our pupils and where appropriate liaise closely with outside agencies to support children with a greater level of need effectively.
The agencies we regularly work closely with are:
At Denham Green E-Act Primary Academy we track pupil progress rigorously. Pupil progress meetings are held regularly to monitor the progress of the SEN and more vulnerable pupils within each year group. This also means that pupils who are not making progress are identified swiftly, interventions are evaluated and other interventions are implemented in order to meet individual needs.
For more detailed information about how the academy support children with additional needs please consult the following documents:
E-ACT Denham Green SEND Policy 2025-2026
E-ACT Denham Green SIR
If you have any concerns about your child regarding special educational needs and/or disability, please feel free to make an appointment with Mrs Kilyan at the academy office.

If you would like help from this service, including independent support please call 01296 383754 or email sendias@buckscc.gov.uk

Sport & Sports Premium Funding
We at Denham Green believe that physical activity not only improves health, reduces stress and improves concentration, but also promotes correct physical growth and development. Denham Green provides enjoyable experiences, where positive attitudes of sensitivity, leadership, co-operation, competition and tolerance may develop. Exercise has a positive influence on academic achievement, emotional stability and interaction with others.
Through sport and other physical activities our children will learn about their responsibilities both as individuals and members of groups and teams. They learn to cooperate and to compete fairly, understanding their own and other’s roles.
Our aim is that; through physical education we teach and develop physical competence, an appreciation of skilled and creative performances, understanding of basic principles of ‘fair play’ and improve interpersonal skills. The Academy will achieve the above through:
· Following a broad and balanced PE curriculum fulfilling the requirements of the National Curriculum.
· Offering swimming lessons in order to provide the opportunity for every child to be able to swim 25m and learn basic water skills (currently offered in the Summer Term in Years 4 and 5).
Developing the fitness of the individual, by ensuring a good pace in lessons and incorporating fitness activities into physical education lessons as appropriate.
· Developing programmes that meet the needs of all the children, providing equal opportunities.
· Involving the community where possible – e.g. Sports Day and clubs.
· We offer both before school and after school clubs which are run by our professional sports coaches.
· All our PE classes are taught by our professional sports coach alongside the teachers.
Sports premium Funding
Schools receive PE and sport premium funding based on the number of pupils in years 1 to 6. Schools must use the funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of PE and sports that you offer. There at Denham Green we use the premium to:
· develop or add to the PE and sport activities that the Academy already offers
· build capacity and capability within the school to ensure that improvements made now will benefit pupils joining the school in future years
There are 5 key indicators that the Academy should expect to see improvement across:
· the engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity – the Chief Medical Officer guidelines recommend that all children and young people aged 5 to 18 engage in at least 60 minutes of physical activity a day, of which 30 minutes should be in school.
· the profile of PE and sport is raised across the Academy as a tool for whole-school improvement
· increased confidence, knowledge and skills of all staff in teaching PE and sport
· broader experience of a range of sports and activities offered to all pupils
· increased participation in competitive sport

pageCache.pageTitle: Our curriculum - Denham Green E-ACT Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Enhance your experience
We use cookies on this site to improve your user experience.
Our curriculum
Whole School Curriculum Map 2024-2025
OUR EARLY YEARS CURRICULUM
The first curriculum your child will encounter on starting school is the Early Years Foundation Stage. In Reception children learn through play (we call this exploring), with a range of opportunities for child-initiated and teacher-led activities. These activities enable your child to learn through a range of play based activities in a safe and secure environment. Free flow play allows children to become independent learners moving between the indoor and outdoor environments as well as having daily activities that are completed in adult led activities.
The curriculum in the Early Years stage consists of prime and specific areas of learning and development. The three prime areas are personal, social and emotional development, physical development and communication and language. There are also four specific areas of learning: literacy, mathematics, understanding the world and expressive art and design.
Our staff teach the children by ensuring challenging, playful opportunities across the prime and specific areas of learning and development allowing them to foster the characteristics of effective early learning which are playing and exploring, active learning and creating and thinking critically.
phonics
Phonics At Denham Green, we teach phonics using a phonics programme called ‘Little Wandle’. The program provides a carefully sequenced path of instruction. Each lesson builds upon the previous one, ensuring that children’s phonics knowledge and skills develop in a coherent and cumulative manner. Children are taught to recognize and produce the sound for each letter (phoneme) and to match it with the corresponding letter or letter combination (grapheme). This foundational skill enables them to decode new words by blending the sounds together. Learning is reinforced by children being given reading books that are closely aligned with the progression of the phonics taught. These books provide children with the opportunity to apply their phonics knowledge and build confidence as they realize they can read entire books by themselves.
Children in EYFS and KS1 have a 30-minute phonics lesson every day.
reading and writing
In EYFS, pupils are invited to investigate the world around them, within themed topics of learning. Within each theme they share a broad range of texts (using high-quality texts selected form the CLPE scheme), learning new vocabulary and developing their comprehension skills. Within the classroom, there are plentiful activities set up where the children are able to explore and be inquisitive whilst developing their communication and language skills, utilising the new vocabulary that has been taught. In Reception, children build on these skills alongside more formal phonics teaching. They also take part in reading and writing activities, developing their letter formation, phonemic awareness, blending and segmenting skills.
Across the rest of the school, children receive daily reading and writing lessons, following the CUSP curriculum. CUSP Reading and Writing is an evidence-informed, carefully sequenced English curriculum, which maps core content in reading and writing across the primary journey,
ensuring that learning is taught and revisited over time so that pupils commit their understanding to the long-term memory. CUSP is guided by evidence-led curriculum structures, such as retrieval, spaced retrieval practice and interleaving. It is underpinned by explicit vocabulary instruction and research-focused pedagogy. CUSP is unapologetically ambitious – the aim is to not only improve outcomes for pupils, but also teacher subject knowledge.
our Maths curriculum
Here at the Academy we teach a ‘mastery’ approach to mathematics, with a greater daily emphasis on developing children’s mathematical fluency, their ability to reason and their problem-solving skills. We also follow the ‘concrete-pictorial-abstract’ approach to developing mathematical learning. Our sequence of learning takes the main learning objectives from the national curriculum and breaks them down into teaching blocks across each term. Time is then built in for maths assessments and for recapping at the end of the term. The topics into which the curriculum is broken down are known as ‘small steps’. The children have a daily maths lesson, which develops these skills, and each lesson contains three parts: ‘Do It’ (which develops the children’s mathematical fluency), ‘Twist It’ (which develops their reasoning skills) and ‘Solve It’ (which develops problem-solving). The children also have additional shorter arithmetical lessons during the week, where we continue to reinforce key skills, and fluency in times tables.
our Science curriculum
Science is taught across the Academy every week as a discrete lesson, using the National Curriculum programmes of study across all classes. Our curriculum has been sequenced so that topics are revisited across the years, with new learning building on prior learning. In every year group we want our children to learn not just the knowledge but also the skills of being a scientist; therefore, wherever we can, science is taught through practical activities and investigations.
our Physical Education curriculum
All children are taught the relationship between physical activity and a healthy body and a healthy mind from an early age. We are so fortunate to have Mr Keen our PE coach work alongside the teachers to deliver two high-quality PE lessons a week, incorporating a weekly ‘Games’ lesson alongside other elements of the curriculum such as dance, gymnastics and athletics. Our end-of-year sports day then culminates in a showcase of the skills the children have learnt across the curriculum. Our PE provision also extends to after school too, as we also offer PE clubs across Key stage 1 and 2, changing the activities each half term.
our computing curriculum
Computing runs through the whole curriculum, as children become familiar with technology through the use of laptops, interactive whiteboards and tablets. We also teach Computing as a discrete lesson, again sequencing our curriculum so that topics are revisited and built on as the children progress though the Academy. Topics covered include understanding computing systems and networks, programming, data handling and creating media, as well as more practical skills such as word processing and using email. Alongside this, and permeating the entire computing curriculum, is engaging children to know how to use technology safely and being aware of how to stay safe online.
our religious education curriculum
At the Academy, we have developed our curriculum alongside the requirements of the Buckinghamshire agreed syllabus. Children are taught RE each week, and across the curriculum children learn about the main world faiths. The way we have sequenced our curriculum is to ensure that these religions are taught more than once, so that the children can use their prior knowledge to make links to new learning, therefore deepening their understanding. As the children revisit and learn new aspects of each faith, the children are taught to respect the beliefs of others; through R.E. we encourage children to reflect on their experiences, behaviour and opinions and in doing so prepare them for life in a diverse society. Parents and carers have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education. Should you wish to do this please speak to the Class Teacher.
our languages curriculum
Pupils from Years 3-6 will receive one French discreet lesson a week. Children will be introduced to key vocabulary that can be used on a daily basis in class, along with singing and playing games. Lessons will also provide the opportunity for pupils to learn about the culture and geography of France.
our music curriculum
Pupils in Early Years use song and music throughout their curriculum, to support learning in all areas. Pupils from Year 1-6 receive a weekly discreet Music lesson covering performance, singing, music theory, history and provides an opportunity for children to listen to Music from a range of different eras and cultures.
We employ the Buckinghamshire Music Trust to come in to the Academy and deliver practical lessons to all classes from Years 1-6, with each year group having a half term of practical instruction with instruments, such as African drumming.
We also offer individual music lessons in drumming, guitar and piano with a peripatetic teacher, which can be booked via the Academy and take place during the school day.
Music Development Plan
our geography curriculum
Geography is taught across Academy half-termly, in parallel with History. In Early Years, the curriculum is matched to the overall topic the children are learning about, and then across Years 1-6 Our Geography curriculum teaches a combination of physical and human geography, incorporating a sequenced development in the children’s knowledge of countries, continents and their locational and place knowledge.
our history curriculum
History is taught across Academy half-termly, in parallel with Geography. In Early Years, the curriculum is matched to the overall topic the children are learning about, and then across Years 1-6 our History curriculum adopts a thematic approach, with the children in each year group following one theme across three different topics each year. In Year 1, the children learn about change over time; in Year 2 they learn about significant event and people; Year 3 will learn about different civilisations; Year 4 will learn about the impact of invaders and settlers on
Britain; Year 5 learn about the impact of change over time; and Year 6 will learn about how individual events caused change.
our Art & Design curriculum
Art & Design is taught across the Academy half-termly, in parallel with Design & Technology. Our Art & Design curriculum balances developing both the children’s key skills and their knowledge and is sequenced so that these are built on and developed each year. The 4 areas of Art & Design these incorporate are Drawing, Painting & Mixed Media, Craft & Design and Sculpture & 3D.
our pshe curriculum
Our PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic) curriculum is taught through the programme of ‘Jigsaw’. There are 6 Jigsaw Puzzles (half-termly units) designed so the whole school can study the same learning themes at the same time, each year group at its own level. The Puzzles are sequential and developmental throughout each academic year. Jigsaw includes regular circle time discussions with the aim to stimulate debate and reflection within a structured setting. Children learn about healthy lifestyles, keeping safe, peer pressure, physical development and relationships, all an essential part of life and learning.

pageCache.text:

Mental health curriculum
We have developed a mental health curriculum to sit alongside our educational curriculum.
Our mental health curriculum was put together with pupils so they are based on real needs. This way children can be encouraged to learn about mental health as part of their everyday classroom experiences.
Post-lockdown, we knew children could not dive straight back into their educational curriculum as it was. Our Relationships and Recovery Curriculum focussed on supporting children to recover from trauma, anxiety and even loss while redeveloping important relationships.

Mental health first aid
If there is only one person in an academy who someone can turn to for support, it becomes a big deal to seek them out.
This is why we have trained over 1,800 youth and adult mental health first aiders across our trust, which is over half our workforce.
First aiders are trained to spot the early signs of a mental health issue. It is our goal to train every member of staff as a mental health first aider.

An E-ACT academy
We are proud to be one of 37 E-ACT academies in England.
Our community includes over 25,000 pupils and 3,500 staff across the country.
What it means to be part of E-ACT
As an E-ACT academy we share ideas with other academies in the trust in ways other schools may not be able to. Our pupils and staff also feel part of something much bigger.
E-ACT academies also have support from people across the trust who help us to make things even better for our children.
In 2026, E-ACT was named Multi-Academy Trust of the Year at the MAT Excellence Awards. In addition, E-ACT Heartlands Academy based in Birmingham, won Secondary School of the Year at the 2026 Tes Schools Awards.
Think big, show team spirit, do the right thing
We believe that young people should never be held back from achieving great things.
By encouraging them to think big and believe that anything is possible, by showing them the importance of team spirit and by supporting them to carefully think through decisions to do the right thing, we know that every one of our pupils can realise their full potential.

Governance Information
E-ACT is a multi-academy trust responsible for the governance and strategic oversight of all E-ACT academies.
The Board of Trustees is accountable for the performance of the Trust and its academies. Trustees set the strategic direction of E-ACT, oversee educational and financial performance, and ensure compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
Through its governance structure, E-ACT provides effective oversight while empowering academy leaders to deliver excellent outcomes for pupils.
Governance at E-ACT
OUR GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
Members: Members act as the guardians of E-ACT’s charitable purpose. They ensure the Trust remains true to its mission and values and are responsible for appointing trustees and approving significant constitutional changes.
Board of Trustees: The Board of Trustees oversees the strategic direction and performance of the Trust. Trustees ensure E-ACT meets its legal obligations, uses public funds responsibly and delivers high-quality education across all academies. They hold the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to account for educational and financial performance.
Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and National Leadership Team: The CEO leads the Trust, supported by the National Leadership Team. Together, they implement the Trust’s strategy, oversee educational, financial and operational performance, and ensure academies receive the support they need to succeed.
Academy Headteachers: Headteachers lead their academies on a day-to-day basis, ensuring high standards of education, safeguarding, behaviour and pupil wellbeing. They work closely with the National Leadership Team to deliver strong outcomes for pupils.
Academy Ambassadors: Academy Ambassadors provide local insight, support and constructive challenge. They help strengthen engagement between the academy, its community and the Trust, but do not hold delegated governance responsibilities.
Scheme of Delegation
Our Scheme of Delegation sets out how decisions are made across our organisation and explains the different layers of governance that work together to support our pupils, staff, and communities. The Scheme of Delegation ensures clarity, accountability and effective governance across all E-ACT academies. VIEW OUR SCHEME OF DELEGATION
Further Information
Further information about E-ACT’s governance arrangements, including statutory governance documents, Trustee information, declarations of interest and annual reports, can be found on the E-ACT website.
If you have any questions about our governance arrangements, please contact the National Governance Team at Governance@E-ACT.org.uk.
Academy Ambassadors
Every E-ACT academy is supported by an Academy Ambassador Group. Ambassador Groups connect academies with their local communities, bringing valuable insight, experience and perspective to support the success of the academy and enrich Trust-wide governance.
E-ACT has established an Ambassador Group in every academy because local voice is essential. Ambassador Groups help ensure that each academy remains connected to its community and that the views of parents, pupils and local stakeholders help inform the Trust’s understanding of academy life.
Ambassador Groups are not governance bodies and do not hold delegated decision-making powers. Their role is to strengthen the partnership between the academy, its community and E-ACT through three key pillars:
Membership
Each Academy Ambassador Group includes the Headteacher and two Parent Ambassadors elected in accordance with E-ACT’s Articles of Association.
Groups may also include individuals from the local community who can contribute their skills, experience, networks and local knowledge to support the academy and its pupils. Membership is designed to reflect the diversity and needs of the academy community while bringing together a broad range of perspectives.
VIEW OUR CURRENT AMBASSADOR GROUP MEMBERSHIP
Ambassador Charter
All Academy Ambassadors are expected to uphold the values of E-ACT and work in accordance with the Ambassador Group Charter, which sets out the commitments and expectations of Ambassadors, academies, the Trust and the Board of Trustees.
Get Involved
We are always keen to hear from parents, carers and members of the local community who are interested in supporting the work of our Academy Ambassador Group.
If you would like to find out more about becoming an Academy Ambassador, please contact the academy directly.
